newsitem.title: ROMANIA: U.S. pension fund to buy Romania trouble bank.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pension fund to buy Romania trouble bank.

text.p: Romania's private troubled bank Dacia Felix SA said on Tuesday U.S. pension fund American National Group would take over its assets and liabilities amid long-awaited plans to reorganise the bank.
A statement from Dacia Felix said the bank signed a contract to transfer its total assets and liabilities to the U.S. company, without giving details on the deal.
It said an auditing company would be hired to assess the transaction.
Dacia Felix officials said American National Group was the administrator of a retirement fund operating in Texas and Delaware in the United States in the real estate sector.

Romania's central bank (BNR) last month stripped Dacia Felix -- once a fast-growing bank now struggling with bad debts of some $200 million -- of its banking licence over its deteriorated financial position.
Central bank (BNR) officials were not immediately available to comment on the Dacia Felix deal.
Dacia Felix challenged the legality of the BNR move and a court of appeal verdict on the case is expected on Wednesday.

Dacia Felix has been awaiting a decision by another court in the Transylvanian city of Cluj on its fate after the central bank lodged a case last year asking legal authorities to decide on the bank's liquidation or reorganisation.
But the bank said it had posted a 33.2 billion lei profit last year after a 642.2 billion 1995 loss and was optimistic about its revival provided a foreign investor should be found.
The contract which the bank announced on Tuesday was subject to approval by the Cluj court and a committee of Dacia Felix creditors.
Not a single bank has been declared bankrupt in Romania since the restructuring of the banking system after the 1989 fall of communism. Forty commercial banks are operating in the Balkan country.
